Convert draw-free mfrmr plot data to ggplot2

Source: R/api-as-ggplot.R, R/api-gpcm-reporting.R
as_ggplot.Rd

plot() returns a ggplot object that can be restyled or composed directly. Use as_ggplot() to convert saved mfrm_plot_data or to select a supported display from an analysis object. Passing an existing ggplot without extra controls returns it unchanged, including user edits.

Usage

as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_design_evaluation'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_design_evaluation_plot_data'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_signal_detection'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_signal_detection_plot_data'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_plot_data'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_slope_intervals'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_curve_intervals'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_gpcm_bootstrap'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_results'
as_ggplot(x, type = NULL, component = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

An mfrm_plot_data object, or an mfrmr object with a draw-free plot method. Corrected-JML slope, location and step plots retain their point or cumulative-distribution view, labels, reference and interpretation note; conversion does not add confidence intervals.

type

Optional plot type passed to plot() for a non-plot-data input. A saved plot-data input already selects a view and rejects type.

component

Optional tabular payload component to convert.

...

Arguments passed to the draw-free plot method. CCC conversion additionally accepts slope_aes, facet_by, and show_overlay. A saved mfrm_plot_data object already contains its view and display settings: it rejects extra arguments (except those three CCC controls for a complete CCC view). To change the level or source plot settings, create a new payload from the fitted model or statistical result. For appearance changes after conversion, use ggplot tools such as ggplot2::labs(title = NULL).

Value

A ggplot2 plot object, with a mfrmr_notes attribute when the source plot payload contains a notes table. Paired Wright/CCC payloads from plot(reference, comparison = comparison) retain their selected comparison or difference view, group selection and monochrome panel policy.

Details

Saved plot conversion retains the selected view, values, intervals, missing states, display settings and interpretation. It does not refit, rescore, recompute diagnostics or change interval qualifications. Use plot_data() for other tables; choosing a component does not authorize a different statistic.

Model and diagnostic views. Dedicated converters cover Wright maps, expected-score/fit pathways, CCCs, bubbles, DIF/DFF, portable scores, testlet and shared-rater results, conditional Person scores and multivariate D-studies.

  • Bubbles keep radii, colours, facet order and reference lines. Relative radii are preserved; base plot units and ggplot physical sizes need not match across devices. Recreate payloads lacking radii/colours with plot(x, type = "bubble").

  • Matched ordinary/extended comparisons retain centered effects, paired or difference views, exclusions and alternative text; see plot.mfrm_extended_comparison().

  • Portable scores use the default or component = "data", preserving axes, endpoints, review symbols and unplotted dispositions.

  • Agreement keeps the chosen exact/correlation/difference metric, pair order, cutoffs, expected overlay and missing pairs. Heatmaps use saved labels, palette and fixed metric scales.

  • Linking keeps drift/wave intervals, cumulative offsets or common counts; unavailable offsets neither become zero nor connect lines across gaps. Drift heatmaps use saved residuals.

  • Threshold sensitivity retains tile/curve views and text alternatives; see plot.mfrm_screening_sensitivity(). Response residuals retain their posterior/plug-in probability target, absent reference cutoffs, and available Infit when Outfit is undefined; see plot.mfrm_response_diagnostics().

  • Testlet/extended score views keep unavailable/prior-only rows, conditional uncertainty, exclusions and alternative text; see plot.mfrm_testlet_scores(). Bootstrap views use arrows for infinite endpoints and dashed ordinary intervals.

G/D-study views. D-studies retain G/Phi or SEM panels, fixed-count groups, units, unavailable estimates, supplied ribbons and gaps; component = "series" uses the same converter. G-studies retain negative points, component intervals and square outlines for unavailable intervals. With an analysis object, intervals = TRUE, assumption = "normal" explicitly computes intervals in its plot method before conversion. Saved plot conversion only reuses them.

Difference-interval plots from mfrm_d_study_comparison return ggplot objects via both plot() and as_ggplot(), with underlying tables accessible through plot_data().

Profiles and exploratory structure. The default and the listed component selectors keep the complete view:

  • Severity ("data"): ordered levels, normal bounds, guide bands, fixed/ unavailable states and precision notes. "Profile" does not mean likelihood profiling or qualify exploratory JML/fallback/regularized uncertainty.

  • Residual PCA ("data"): scree/reference/excess/loadings, saved eigenvalues, cutoffs, signed loadings and encodings; method IDs are not plotted variables.

  • External-feature PCA ("table"): selected axes, retained-component symbols, group colours/shapes, labels and transformations. Score axes have equal units; loadings are coefficients, not correlations.

  • Dendrograms ("tree"): merges, heights, leaf order, labels and group boxes, including tied-height cuts. Heights are not significance or branch support.

  • Imputation co-membership ("matrix"): all-imputation denominator, ID order, fixed [0,1] scale, legend/labels and imputation count. Gray crossed cells are unavailable; zero is a valid fraction. Partitions are not pooled.

  • Silhouettes ("table"): widths on [-1,1], saved order and overall mean. Numeric profiles keep original-unit means/medians/counts with offset symbols; categorical profiles keep category order, unused levels, counts and within-group proportions on [0,1] ("table" or "matrix"). These summaries do not estimate uncertainty, rater quality or sampling stability.

Main-effects mfrm_d_study plots retain the selected design comparison through their dedicated conversion; use plot_data() for its tables.

Interval displays. Fit-measure measure_ci views keep facet/level rows, saved normal endpoints (including exploratory JML), notes, open diamonds for fixed targets and crosses for unavailable intervals (component = "table"). Pooled fixed-facet MI uses the same selector, retaining t endpoints, df, contrasts and complete-data information cautions. It additionally marks infinite bounds with arrows; arrow tips are display limits, not finite bounds.

Selecting component must preserve the selected view. Use plot_data() to extract other tables and specify their axes and grouping in custom graphics. Residual Q-Q conversion retains the saved quantile axes with the default or component = "data"; it adds no normality test. Residual-correlation heatmaps keep the same facet on both axes, scale [-1,1], gray unavailable cells, overlap counts and interpretation notes. Rating-scale and category-structure displays keep selected counts/thresholds, missing outcomes, expected-count overlay and palette; use the default or matching category_table/threshold_table. Thresholds are points; stored SEs/CI-use flags do not become curve or gap intervals.

Category-curve bundles (including their overview), category-structure boundary views and threshold ladders also use dedicated conversion to retain their distinct curve targets and selected view. Fitted CCC plots from plot(fit, type = "ccc") retain their dedicated conversion.

Bias scatter/ranked views preserve their axes, saved review rules and conditional interval bounds, including dashed search-limited bounds. Bias heatmaps, histograms and facet profiles have dedicated conversions that retain the selected layout and screening settings. Halo distributions, selected per-rater summaries and signed retained-edge matrices preserve the selected metric, missing comparisons and caveats. Halo network conversion retains the saved graph layout and edges. Save the complete analysis result and recreate its plot for current notes.

Shrinkage plots from plot(fit, type = "shrinkage") preserve both estimates for each facet level, their adjustment direction and saved descriptive bands. Use the default or component = "data". Conversion does not turn plug-in bands into calibrated confidence intervals. Recreate older plots from a fit with a refreshed shrinkage report first.

Other draw-free payloads use a conservative tabular fallback; inspect plot_data_components() when automatic inference is not appropriate. Titles, subtitles and captions are omitted by default and retained as metadata. Use plot_data(p, "notes") to retrieve descriptions and cautions. Explicitly enabled text is wrapped at 72 columns; use ggplot2::labs() for custom labels or narrower exports. Fit plots created with show_title = FALSE or show_notes = FALSE retain those settings on conversion. To set them when converting a fit directly, pass the flags through .... Interpretation and display notes remain available in attr(plot, "mfrmr_notes"), when present in the source payload. Wright, pathway, and CCC conversions share the fit-family series palette, honour monochrome presets and supplied palette overrides, and preserve line-type or point-shape distinctions. CCC categories retain their source order. When slope_aes = "colour", slopes instead use a continuous viridis scale (a grey gradient in monochrome); categories still have line types.

Fixed-facet RSM/PCM intervals retain the selected covariance method, level, status symbols and optional ordinary comparison. Titles, subtitles, captions, reference lines and legends can be changed through the source plot arguments. Methods use both line types and vertical offsets, including in monochrome.

Interactive views

The visual gallery shows how to pass a supported ggplot to plotly::ggplotly() for browser-based hovering, zooming and legend filtering. Plotly is an optional downstream renderer. Keep the original mfrmr plot and its plot_data() notes alongside the widget; conversion does not recalculate estimates or intervals. Check labels, custom geoms and interval layers after conversion. The gallery includes static figures, numeric tables and an HTML export recipe.

See also

mfrmr_output_guide() with scope = "plots" for selected purpose-based routes, conversion status and alternatives.

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("as_ggplot", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
# A balanced slice retains every Rater and Criterion while running quickly.
toy <- toy[toy$Person %in% unique(toy$Person)[1:12], , drop = FALSE]
fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person",
                c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score", maxit = 30)
as_ggplot(fit, type = "wright")
as_ggplot(fit, type = "fit_pathway", include_person = TRUE)
as_ggplot(plot(fit, type = "ccc", draw = FALSE))
} # }
